# onetoeight

> A free practical guide and a weekly meetup that build eight essentials into the lives of young people aged 13 to 23.

onetoeight exists for a screen-born generation: the most connected and the most adrift. It publishes a free guide, a weekly online meetup and practical resources covering eight foundations, written for young people and useful to the parents, teachers, youth leaders and community workers around them.

## The free guide (Universal edition)

The Universal edition is secular, written for every background, belief and tradition, and free to read and adapt. Every page carries spoken-word audio. The guide pages are public and indexed, so they can be found and linked directly.

- [Introduction and contents](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal): Start here. What the eight essentials are, and why roots matter.
- [The ability to sit in silence](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-one-universal): Make room to notice before adding more input.
- [Your body is a home](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-two-universal): Care for the body you actually have.
- [Useful skills for real life](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-three-universal): Feed yourself, fix safely, make things and understand money.
- [Digital self-defence](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-four-universal): Protect your attention, privacy, accounts and identity.
- [Real community](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-five-universal): Build belonging without turning friendship into a score.
- [Knowledge you can carry](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-six-universal): Use the internet without outsourcing your mind.
- [Make room for the outside](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-seven-universal): Go gently, notice more and adapt nature to your life.
- [Test what you believe](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/essential-eight-universal): Examine convictions and stay open to evidence.
- [Reading & Resources](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/reading-resources): Free, well-chosen next steps, one for each essential. Scan or tap to open each link.
- [Activities](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/activities): Hands-on things to try, one category for each essential. Pick one and do it this week.
    - [Bonus extras](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/bonus-extras): A discount code for the Afterschool Agent, the paid programme, and the free local studio.
- [Discussion questions](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/discussion-questions): Ready-to-run conversations for youth groups, schools and community settings.
- [Changelog](https://www.onetoeight.org/guide/universal/changelog): What changed in this edition, and why.

## Site

- [Home](https://www.onetoeight.org/): One to eight: eight essentials for a screen-born generation.
- [About](https://www.onetoeight.org/about.html): Who onetoeight is for and why it exists.
- [For young people](https://www.onetoeight.org/young-people.html): A short starting point written directly to the reader.
- [Afterschool Agent and weekly meetup](https://www.onetoeight.org/afterschool-agent.html): On-demand training plus a live Q&A every Tuesday at 5pm. $44.88 one-time, lifetime access. No subscription.
- [For parents: fear](https://www.onetoeight.org/parents/fear.html): What fear does to a young person, and what helps.
- [For parents: hope](https://www.onetoeight.org/parents/hope.html): Building hope that survives a bad week.
- [For parents: bridge](https://www.onetoeight.org/parents/bridge.html): Staying in conversation across a gap in worldview.
- [Engage](https://www.onetoeight.org/engage/index.html): Essays on attention, meaning, asking better questions and what young people need.
